description: A free-text rejection about noise must become a structured constraint that produces a materially different, visibly responsive next proposal — not a random re-roll.

initialProposal.reasoning: Best-rated candidate; nothing in any profile ruled out a loud venue before this cycle.

rejection.text: It's too loud for me, I want somewhere quieter.

expected.reasoning: The rejection is not a blanket 'no' — it names atmosphere specifically, so the Constraint Updater (A7) writes `noiseLevel: "quiet"` as a correction on Shani's `ParticipantMeetingContext` for this meeting, not as an edit to her profile: she has not become someone who always wants quiet, she wants quiet tonight. The next proposal must visibly respond to that. Quiet Corner is the only remaining candidate whose own `soft.noiseLevel` is "quiet", so it is the only materially different, on-topic follow-up, even though it is rated slightly lower than the rejected option. Quiet Corner shuts at midnight while the group is free until 01:00, so the evening ends at midnight — the slot is the intersection, 21:00-00:00, which is exactly the three-hour minimum. Beer Bazaar staying open until 02:00 buys it nothing here: the objection was about noise, not about closing time.
